newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Discount Bank Q3 net up.
newsitem.headline: Israel Discount Bank Q3 net up.

text.p: Israel Discount Bank, Israel's third-largest bank.
The bank has been requested by the government to assist in publishing a prospectus for February 1997 for a public offering of part of the government's shares.

"The board of directors of the bank has decided to raise, concurrently with the state's offering, up to 300 million shekels by issuing subordinated capital notes to the public in Israel. This will expand the bank's operational base and improve its capital ratio," the bank said in a statement.

The bank attributed the rise in net income to an expansion of operations, especially in the area of credit to the public and also from the influence of the gap between the "actual" and "known" consumer price index (CPI).

The decline in operating and other income was due to a reduction of transactions of customers in the capital market, a fall in stock prices, and a decrease in fees from the management of provident funds caused by a decline in their value.
On the other hand, there was a rise in income from expansion of other banking services.
The bank's consolidated assets rose to 76.3 billion shekels at the end of September from 73.0 billion on September 30, 1995.

"The moderate rise in all assets, despite a significant expansion in operations, is mainly a result of the lag in rates of foreign currency compared to the rise in the CPI for the period under review," the statement said. About half of the bank's assets are denominated in or linked to foreign currency.
Credit to the public as of September 30 totalled 42.5 billion shekels against 38.6 billion a year earlier while deposits from the public rose to 64.8 billion from 59.9 billion.
Shareholders' equity on September 30 stood at 4.1 billion shekels, against 3.9 billion a year earlier.
The ratio of shareholders' equity to total risk assets was 8.7 percent, similar to the end of 1995.

The bank's major subsidiary, Israel Discount Bank of New York, is the largest Israeli-owned bank operating overseas. Its balance sheet as of September 30 amounted to $3.75 billion, shareholders' equity stood at $343.1 million and income for the first nine months reached $18.3 million.
